title: Book Three · Chapter 20: Mum's New Bag
story:
By late autumn, Mum has a small pile of cloth beside her chair.

On Sunday, she spreads the pieces across the table. One green piece is from her trip to the shops with her friend. Ronan remembers the pears from that afternoon.

“Is that for a customer?” he asks.

“For me. A new bag.”

She puts a long grey piece beside the green one.

“What happened to the yellow cloth?”

“It stayed in the shop. I still have my money.”

“This one will be green and grey?”

“Yes.”

Ronan sits down. Mum moves her scissors away from his elbow and measures the cloth.

“I can hold that end,” he says.

She gives him the end of the tape. He holds it against one corner while she checks the length.

“Is the bag for your books?”

“Sometimes. And small things from the shops.”

“Four pieces of bread?”

“Those can stay in the old bag.”

She draws a short line on the cloth. Ronan lets go of the tape.

Outside, Dad is cleaning his work shoes. He has put a newspaper under them. A little dirt falls from one heel.

“Is that mine?” he calls through the door.

“No,” Mum says.

“I only asked.”

“You need to ask before I finish it.”

Dad comes to the doorway with a brush in one hand. He looks at the green cloth.

“It would not suit my shoes.”

Mum laughs and starts to cut.

Ronan goes into the yard. He brings his school bag out and empties it on the bench. Old paper fills the bottom. There is a dry leaf between two books.

He takes out a small paper tray. One side is crushed. He presses it flat and puts it beside the books.

Dad looks over.

“For your lunch?”

“Maths counters.”

Ronan shows him the folded sides. Dad turns the tray over, then gives it back.

“You need thicker paper for heavy things.”

“These are small.”

“Then keep that paper.”

Ronan puts his books back in order. He keeps the tray flat inside one cover.

Later, Mum calls him to the table. The bag has two sides now, but no straps.

She holds a strip of grey cloth against her shoulder.

“Here?”

Ronan looks. “A little longer.”

She lowers it and checks again.

“Better.”

Mum marks the place herself. She holds the strip against the green cloth.

“Is it too narrow?” Ronan asks.

“For books, yes. This is only the length.”

She folds a wider piece over her shoulder. She lifts her arm and moves it forward.

Ronan watches the cloth move.

“Does that feel better?”

“It does. I need room here too.”

She puts a hand beside her arm. Then she takes the strip down and checks her mark again.

She lays everything aside and takes out three cups.

Dad leaves his clean shoes by the door. They drink tea at the table before Mum starts the next part.

Ronan moves his school bag off the spare chair. Mum puts her new green and grey pieces there, safely away from the cups.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

pile＝一堆；tape＝卷尺（本章语境）；heel＝鞋跟；strap＝带子。

## 理解问题

1. Mum这次为谁做包？她有没有买下之前觉得贵的黄色布？
2. Ronan怎样帮忙确定尺寸？最后由谁标记肩带长度？

## 读句子

**She gives him the end of the tape.**

拆开看：She / gives him / the end of the tape.

她／把一端交给他／交给他卷尺的一端。
